cards.note: Converted to an npm bundle: dsh.bundle.patch -> cordis.patch.yml, dsh.client web half, exports './client'; installed only through `dsh plugin --profile web add` (README.md). The repository-plugin route and its unsafe publish procedure are gone.

The package already declares the merged dsh.client ({platform: web}); there is no legacy dshClient field and no dsh.plugin.json, and the packed declaration is what the live boot manifest row was composed from.
dsh.client {platform: web, inject[]} plus exports['./client'] are declared, so the client-modules scan picks the out-of-tree package up; verified live (window.__DSH_BOOT__ row id == package name).
Every service the body reads is declared in inject (slots, sessions, workspaces, locale, remote, remote.directoryPicker); the composition smoke check asserts only declared services are read.

No optional service: sessions/workspaces/remote.directoryPicker/locale/slots are guaranteed by the web profile, so hard inject entries are correct and a missing one must fail loud rather than degrade.
No session/event subscription remains in either half: the old session/title write-behind is retired (the base bundle owns title persistence) and the browser half reads controllers, not event streams.

The browser half consumes the shipped ISessions client service for list/search/open/fork and derives no session mood/waiting/completion state, so no Node-half aggregation plus /state route is required.
The plugin never tails task/run output, so the tasks.peek removal does not touch it.
No httpServer/tasks/onTaskDone usage anywhere; the host half has no service reads at all.
The plugin handles no image attachments or image metadata.
The plugin neither registers, wraps, parses nor snapshot-tests read_image.
No LLM adapter, image interceptor, or attachment cache is involved.
No Host APIProxy call site: the browser half reaches the Host only through the public ctx.remote.directoryPicker namespace.
Required only when the target is exactly alpha.1; the target is alpha.2 (A2-01 restored the retention semantics) and this package writes no persisted session events.
No host source patch and no imports from internal session-view paths; the plugin lives entirely on public slot/service seams.
The plugin reads no profile files; install and verification use the official launcher path (dsh plugin --profile web add, dsh --profile web --dump-config) with the runtime DSH_HOME.
Not a headless wrapper and no stdout/stderr parsing exists in the package.
The plugin uses no tool presentation mode, PTC preset, or dispatch waterfall.
Not a permission/approval/WebFetch-policy plugin; no tools pre-execute policy is registered.
No custom HTTP/WS/RPC or /api routes: dsh-client-modules serves the bundle, and the acceptance check used the printed token URL, its 303, and the HttpOnly cookie.
Not a model provider plugin, so the model-settings login capability does not apply.
The plugin registers its own dictionary namespace through the ordinary ctx.locale.register API; it adds no third-party language and carries no i18n patch.
No subagent orchestration or selector surface in this package.
Informational for deployments on the official DeepSeek adapter; the plugin needs no code change and states no privacy posture.
No PowerShell/Bash-persistence or Windows directory-picker workaround survives: the only old workaround (patching the official dist bundle in place) was dropped with the overlay rebase.
The deployment does not enable session-log-deepseek and the plugin has no egress path.

Acceptance follows the target recipe: install into the web profile, dsh web --no-open, exchange the printed token URL for the cookie, read window.__DSH_BOOT__.entries by package name, then request the entry's /plugins bundle; no URL or path is hardcoded.
No structured-question answerer is registered, so the userQuestions.registerProvider removal does not touch the plugin.
The plugin never infers an agent preset from a persisted session and sets no agent-presets roots.
No first-token/TPS logic, so isTokenDelta is not imported.
The bundle composes over dsh-base but restates no telemetry row and takes no privacy stance, so nothing needs overriding for session-telemetry-otel or the package-inventory row.
The plugin does not import @earendil-works/pi-ai and depends on no provider package.

The removed @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime/client type entry and its dsh.client.inject/peer rows are gone; the client context is @deepseek-ai/cordis and the domain services come from the per-domain client packages.

The served bundle registers the factory under the package name (window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id: '@bench/dsh-bench-workspace-ya'})), matching the package name, the boot-manifest entry id, and the Loader row; verified in the live manifest.
The takeover reads Session Controller list rows, not conversation-node timelines or user-message content, so no SessionBinding durable event window is needed.
The plugin does not touch the composer (no draft injection, history recall, shortcuts, or selection code).
No MarkdownText/fenced CodeBlock rendering; the component bodies render session rows and the picker only.
No ctx.connection.api use: session rows come from the Session Controller and directory operations from the Remote namespace, both public services.
The plugin builds no subagent descriptors and asserts no descriptor version.

ctx.workspaces.startSession is replaced by the uiWorkspace service (list/CRUD stay on ctx.workspaces); because the takeover disables the official provider, the plugin provides UiWorkspace again for ui-sidebar/ui-conversation/ui-agent-preset and the directory pickers.
The plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents, and the target alpha.2 already restores ignorable retention semantics.
Each remote.directoryPicker call resolves RemoteResult and branches on ok, raising a descriptive error from the RemoteFailure code/message instead of treating failures as values.

Dead cohort peers (@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime, @deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants, react, unscoped cordis) are replaced by the packages the browser half consumes, optional, at ^0.1.2-alpha.2 (cordis ^4.0.0-rc.7); the fixture has no lockfile, so the profile's pnpm hoisted linker is the single package manager.
No Node-range workaround exists in the package; the runtime check ran on Node 24.21.0, outside the fixed 24.0-24.11.1 window.
The plugin does not consume pluginInventory/list and validates no PluginInventorySnapshot.
No host.describe call and no Host home/loopback fact in the documented injected face; ctx.remote.$host.home/isLoopback stays the public seam if the browser ever needs it.

The retired write-behind registered no projection unit and the package now needs no sessionProjections inject/peer; @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-title and -projection-cache (dsh-base rows) own the title unit, and the host row exists only to carry the browser half.
The plugin registers, reads, or writes no settings namespace, so the compile-time SettingsNamespaceInput change does not touch it.
